title: Why the Planner Skips an Index
description: Half the rows in a large table have is_active=true. A query returns most columns for all active rows, and EXPLAIN chooses a sequential scan despite an is_active index. What is the sound interpretation?

options.explanation: Equality is a normal B-tree use. The issue here is how many rows the predicate selects.

options.text: The query is automatically covered by the boolean index.
options.explanation: The index lacks most selected columns, and index-only scans also depend on engine visibility conditions.

options.text: Force the index because indexed access is always cheaper.
options.explanation: Fetching many scattered table rows through pointers can cost more than reading the table sequentially.

options.text: Low selectivity can make a scan cheaper; measure before adding or forcing indexes.
options.explanation: Matching a predicate is not enough. Row count, I/O and returned columns affect the plan, while every additional index still costs writes and storage.
